doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Where does your sound come from; hearing yourself
summary: Nobody could say where sound comes from; Miles said it is like sweat. Live sound goes away from you, on headphones it comes at you.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well yeah. One of them is where does your sound come from. Where does your style come from. I asked everybody that. And nobody knew, nobody could answer the question. Miles came closest, he said, “Oh man, my sound, it’s like your sweat.” It’s like your sweat. So I asked everybody where your sound comes from and where your style comes from. And it makes sense that nobody could answer that because you can’t really see yourself or hear yourself the way other people do. As a matter of fact that’s one of the really big takeaways from the recording experiences that I’ve had is that when you’re playing live in the world, the sound goes away from you. Whether you’re a trumpet player, a piano player, saxophone player — it’s going that way. But when you’re recording and you have earphones on, the sound is coming this way. And it’s a very different perspective. You tend to say to yourself wait a minute, I don’t sound like that. But of course that’s exactly how you sound, you just haven’t heard it.
I have to say that reminds me of — I just had a flashback to when I was a kid and the first time I heard my own voice on a recording — “Oh, that can’t be me.”
Was it intimidating at first, with that experience? Like this is really what I sound like ‘cause it’s coming back to my head, and I’m not sure I like it.
